summary: In August 2025 the White House named the National Air and Space Museum among eight Smithsonian museums ordered to review content under Executive Order 14253. In January 2026 the Smithsonian handed over exhibition label photographs.

The state opened the Grand People's Study House in April 1982 for Kim Il Sung's 70th birthday as its national library and centre of Juche studies. Kim portraits hang throughout. Staff control access to materials.

Kim Il Sung founded the exhibition in 1946. It became the Three Revolutions Exhibition in 1983 and was enlarged in 1993. It presents industrial, agricultural and scientific achievements as successes of Juche ideology.
The hall opened in April 2002 to display flowers named after Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il. Festivals on the leaders' birthdays show arrangements from state bodies beside rocket and satellite models.

The palace opened in 1989 under the Korean Youth Corps. Children perform regularly for tourists, singing and dancing in praise of the nation's achievements. KCNA reports the performances as pledges of loyalty to the leaders.

Abdoulaye Wade commissioned the monument, built by North Korea's Mansudae Overseas Projects and inaugurated on 3 April 2010. Wade claimed 35 percent of tourist revenue as intellectual property. Critics called it a presidential vanity project.
